newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - C&W bides time as suitors circle.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - C&W bides time as suitors circle.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Plc (C&W), Britain's second biggest telecommuncations company, said on Wednesday that despite the appeal of its businesses for global alliances, it was biding its time on chosing any partners.

Reporting record full year pre-tax profits of 1.42 billion stg which met analysts' expectations, finance director Robert Lerwill told Reuters the group was still in talks with suitors such as the Global One alliance of Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and America's Sprint Corp.
But he noted: "There's nothing specific on any conversations with Global One worth commenting on.

"People have been approaching us and are interested in us -- which demonstrates our global reach and the appeal we have for many of these global alliances. So we continue, as appropriate, to have (dialogues)."
Global One is keen to gain access to the British market as well as C&W's Asian business interests including its ace card -- a near-60 percent stake in lucrative Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd.

Hong Kong Telecom contributed just over 1.0 billion stg to annual operating profits and 2.67 billion pounds to group turnover of 6.05 billion stg. Turnover including C&W's share of associates came in at just over 7.0 billion stg, a 13 percent rise over last year.

Despite owning a small subsidiary called Cable and Wireless Europe, C&W has limited access to the key European telecoms market, such as France and Germany, which are heading for liberalisation next year.
"If we did in some way get associated with another alliance, then (continental) Europe is the place where there is more to go for," Lerwill said.
C&W says it will use its new, majority-owned cable venture -- Cable and Wireless Communications -- as its springboard for European expansion.

One question mark which hangs over C&W is its holding in Hong Kong Telecom. With only weeks to go before the former British colony revers to Chinese control, speculation has been sparked that China may pressure C&W into reducing its majority stake.

C&W, which says that there is no requirement for it do so, welcomed more direct Chinese State involvement in Hong Kong Telecom last week, seeing it as an expression of faith that the Chinese would use the company as their principal telecoms partner in Hong Kong.
China Everbright, which reports to China's State Council, bought a 7.7 percent stake in the Hong Kong company from CITIC Pacific, which is seen by analysts to be more independent.

Analysts are expecting further Chinese investment in Hong Kong Telecom, combined with new opportunities for the Hong Kong company on the Chinese mainland, which is expected to yield huge potential growth prospects.

"The potential for growth in China is indisputable, although the ability to make attractive returns from investment in that growth maybe a tough proposition," says Adrian Goodall, telecoms analyst at SBC Warburg.
What is clear is that C&W is keen to ensure that any deals with China will be commercially advantageous to its shareholders.
Asked whether C&W or Hong Kong Telecom were in talks with other mainland Chinese companies such as MPT, the powerful Chinese Telecoms Ministry, Lerwill said only:

"You wouldn't expect Hong Kong Telecom from an operating point of view not to be in constant contact with its closest telecom neighbour -- which is China. We talk to many people. But it wouldn't be helpful to anybody to go down any speculative paths more than that."
